qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture nine. Batch and online machine learning. How a model learns from all the data, or as it arrives.
A courier app predicts minutes as w times kilometres.
A courier app predicts minutes = w × km.
One test trip was one kilometre, and took four minutes.
This trip: 1 km in 4 minutes.
Guess w is seven. That is three minutes off, so the cost is nine.
Guess w = 7: 3 minutes off, so the cost is 9.
Every guess has a cost, and together they make a bowl.
Every guess has a cost: together they make a bowl.
At the bottom, w is four. That is the best weight.
The bottom, w = 4, is the best weight.
At w equals ten, the slope is twelve. It points uphill.
The slope shows which way is uphill: 12 at w = 10.
So step the other way. Ten minus zero point two five times twelve is seven.
Step against it: 10 − 0.25 × 12 = 7.
Here the slope is smaller, so the next step is smaller too.
The slope is smaller now, so each step is smaller too.
Ten, seven, five point five. Each step halves the distance to four.
10, 7, 5.5, 4.75, 4.375: the distance halves.
The ball settles at the bottom, near w equals four.
The ball settles at the bottom, w = 4.
Same bowl, same start, and three learning rates.
Same bowl, same start, three learning rates.
Each step is the learning rate times the slope.
Each step is learning rate × slope.
One point one is too big. Each jump lands further out, and it diverges.
1.1 is too big: each jump lands further out. It diverges.
Zero point seven five jumps past the bottom, but still settles.
0.75 jumps past the bottom but still settles.
Zero point one is safe but slow. It creeps down.
0.1 is safe but slow: it creeps down.
Four trips, and the model starts at w equals six.
Four trips; the model starts at w = 6.
The forward pass predicts every trip and measures each error.
Forward pass: predict every trip and measure the error.
The backward pass turns the errors into one gradient, eighteen.
Backward pass: the errors make one gradient, 18.
One update, with rate zero point zero five, takes w from six to five point one.
That was one epoch. Epoch two takes w to four point six zero five.
That was one epoch. Epoch 2 takes w to 4.605.
Full batch uses all the data, so it gets the true gradient.
Full batch uses all the data: the true gradient.
The model learned four minutes per kilometre.
The model learned 4 minutes per km.
Then come roadworks, and each kilometre now takes about six.
Then roadworks: each km now takes about 6.
The model still says four. At four kilometres, it is eight minutes off.
The model still says 4: 8 minutes off at 4 km.
The world changed, not the model. That is concept drift.
The world changed, not the model: concept drift.
One fix is retraining. Each week adds two gigabytes of data.
Each week adds 2 GB of new data.
Retrain on all of it, and week ten reads twenty gigabytes.
Retrain on all of it: week 10 reads 20 GB.
The pile keeps growing every week.
The pile keeps growing every week.
Week thirty-three needs sixty-six gigabytes, more than the sixty-four of memory.
Week 33 needs 66 GB: more than the 64 GB of memory.
So train on recent data only. Four weeks is eight gigabytes, and it fits.
Recent data only: the last 4 weeks, 8 GB each time.
Twenty-four trips, one epoch, and three batch sizes.
24 trips, one epoch, three batch sizes.
One at a time makes an update after every trip.
One at a time: an update after every trip.
Batches of eight update once every eight trips.
Batches of 8: an update after every 8 trips.
Small batches only estimate the gradient, so they are noisy. Some steps go uphill.
Small batches are noisy: some steps go uphill.
The full batch takes one step, with the true gradient.
Full batch: one step, with the true gradient.
After one epoch, the losses are about one hundred and thirty-three, thirty-three, and one point nine.
After one epoch the losses are 133, 33 and 1.9.
On a stream, records arrive one at a time.
On a stream, records arrive one at a time.
Each one makes one small update. Here w goes from four to four point three six.
Each one makes one small update: 4 → 4.36.
Then the record is gone. One pass, and nothing is stored.
Then the record is gone: one pass, nothing stored.
The model keeps adjusting. This is stochastic gradient descent.
Always adjusting: this is stochastic gradient descent.
Two online models learn from the same stream.
Two online models learn from the same stream.
At record forty, roadworks start. Each kilometre now takes six, not four.
Roadworks at record 40: each km now takes 6, not 4.
The faster rate catches up in two records. The slower one needs twenty-three.
Rate 0.02 catches up in 2 records; 0.004 needs 23.
But a fast learner trusts every record.
But a fast learner trusts every record.
One bad record logs two kilometres as ninety minutes. The weight jumps to ten point five nine.
One bad record, 90 min for 2 km: w jumps to 10.59.
Bad data hits at once, so watch online models closely.
Bad data hits at once: watch online models closely.
Covariate shift. The inputs change, like faces in masks.
Covariate shift: the inputs change, like faces in masks.
Prior probability shift. The symptoms stay the same. Before, twelve in twenty had flu.
Prior probability shift: same symptoms; before, 12 in 20 had flu.
In the pandemic, only four in twenty.
In the pandemic, only 4 in 20.
Concept drift. The rule itself changes, from four to six per kilometre.
Concept drift: the rule itself changes, 4 → 6 per km.
Each one makes a trained model decay.
Each one makes a trained model decay.
Step downhill, by the learning rate times the slope.
Learn from all the data, mini-batches, or one record at a time.
Online models adapt as data drifts. Watch for bad data.
